2 indicator, parking signal or any parking precaution parked the lorry at center road.
Due to said impact, the petitioner in MVC No.3451/2019 hit to the said lorry and both the said petitioner sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident,
the petitioner were shifted to Ashwini Hospital, Yelahanka Bangalore and later took treatment at ARS Hospital, Tirpur wherein they took treatment as an inpatient and spent huge amount.

The petitioner in MVC No.3451/2019, prior to the accident was working as owner cum driver of the lorry and earning Rs.25,000/- per month and the petitioner in MVC No.3452/2019 was working as a cleaner and earning Rs.20,000/- per month.

There is nothing on record to show that the charge-sheet filed by the police is defective or collusive.

Moreover, it is settled law that the term "rashness and negligence" has to be construed lightly while deciding a petition for claim of compensation under the MV Act as compare to the word "rashness and negligence" as finds mention in the Indian Penal Code.
This is because the provisions of M.V.Act dealing with compensation are benevolent legislation and not a penal one.

Therefore, on over all appreciation of evidence, I am of the opinion that the accident occurred due to the negligence of driver of Lorry bearing reg.No.RJ-11-JB-1094 which belongs to the respondent No.1 and respondent No.2 is its insurer.

opennyai_summary.facts:
The claim petition in MVC.No.3451/2019 and MVC.No.3452/2019 has filed by the respective petitioner u/s.166 of Motor Vehicle Act, claiming compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- and Rs.30,00,000/- respectively with interest from the date of petition till its realization for injuries sustained by him in a Road Traffic Accident.
The petitioner in MVC No.3451/2019, prior to the accident was working as owner cum driver of the lorry and earning Rs.25,000/- per month and the petitioner in MVC No.3452/2019 was working as a cleaner and earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
The Gudibande police have registered a criminal case against the driver of the lorry bearing reg.No.RJ-11-JB-1094 in crime No.85/2019 under Section 279 and 337 of IPC .
The The respondent No.1 is the Owner and the respondent No.2 is the insurer of lorry bearing reg.No.RJ-11-JB-1094 and the insurance policy was in force.
Hence both respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation in said both cases.
Hence these petitions.
3. After service of notice in both the petitions, the respondent No.1 and Respondent No.2 appeared through their respective advocate and only respondent No.2 has filed its written statement in both the cases.
It has denied the age, income and avocation of the petitioner in both the cases.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled Rs.2,85,600/-
under the head of loss of future earning capacity.
opennyai_summary.issue:
4. On the basis of aforesaid pleadings, this Tribunal has framed the following issues: -
 COMMON ISSUES
1. Whether the petitioner proves that, he  sustained injuries due to RTA which took  place on 18.04.2019 when he was going  Beechagana halli cross, NH - 7 road,
 Chikkaballapura in his Ashok Leyland Lorry  bearing No.TN-39-CD-1341 at about 2.00 am.,
 and a lorry bearing No.RJ-11-JB-1094 was  parked carelessly at Center of the road  without any indications due to which  petitioners vehicle dashed against respondent  vehicle and petitioner sustained grievous  injuries as alleged in the petition ?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for  compensation?
If so, what is the quantum?
What Order or Award?
for the following:
 REASONS
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
There is nothing on record to show that the charge-sheet filed by the police is defective or collusive.
Moreover, it is settled law that the term "rashness and negligence" has to be construed lightly while deciding a petition for claim of compensation under the MV Act as compare to the word "rashness and negligence" as finds mention in the Indian Penal Code.
This is because the provisions of M.V.Act dealing with compensation are benevolent legislation and not a penal one.
Therefore, on over all appreciation of evidence, I am of the opinion that the accident occurred due to the negligence of driver of Lorry bearing reg.No.RJ-11-JB-1094 which belongs to the respondent No.1 and respondent No.2 is its insurer.
Hence, in all the Tribunal is of the view that the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.76,190/- is just and reasonable towards Medical expenses.
Considering the said fact the Tribunal is of the view that compensation of Rs.1,000/- per day for 9 days and also by including conveyance, a sum of Rs.12,000/- is just and reasonable towards food extra Raghu Rajgopal vs Deepak Gupta on 5 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/124173989/
9 nourishment, conveyance and medical attendant charges.
Under such circumstances, the age of petitioner was considered as 29  (SCCH-9) MVC.No.3451/2019  15 c/w MVC.No.3452/2019 years and same is taken into consideration for applying multiplier and the proper multiplier is "17" is applicable as per Smt.Sarala Verma's case.
By considering the facts and circumstances of the case, the Tribunal is of the view that compensation of Rs.50,000/- is just and reasonable to under the head of deprivation of future amenities.
Therefore by considering the injury and facts and circumstances of the case the Tribunal is of the view that the compensation of Rs.50,000/- is just and reasonable towards pain and sufferings.
The petitioner has claimed compensation towards medical expenses.
Considering the said fact the Tribunal is of the view that compensation of Rs.1,000/- per day for 9 days and also by including conveyance, a sum of Rs.12,000/- is just and reasonable towards food extra nourishment, conveyance and medical attendant charges.
The Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, fixed notional income of the year 2019 at 14,000/- p.m.,
Accordingly, the notional income of petitioner during the year 2019 treated as Rs.14,000/- p.m.
Considering the age, nature of injuries, treatment given & duration of his stay in the hospital, it is quite natural that petitioner could not have carried out his avocation normally for at least 2 months.
Thus, by taking into account the notional income of PW.1, this Tribunal awards Rs.42,000/- (14,000/- X 3)
towards loss of income during treatment period.
